paras: The inner child, the guards, and the three inner adults

Your inner child won’t trust you right away. It’s not going to be enough for you to meditate, say three nice sentences to the inner child and expect to have its trust. What’s going to help your inner child to trust you is you, as a person that you are right now.

In this post I am going to talk about what you need to develop in yourself in order to be able to reparent your inner child. I’m going to talk about it in terms of three aspects: your Nurturer, your Protector and your Leader/Guru, but I don’t mean them as if there were really three people in you. It’s you that needs to develop these qualities.

Also, your inner child’s worth is not dependent on these qualities… It has its own worth, and its own qualities, like playing, being tender, not taking life too seriously, being creative and wondering at the world.
When the adult role is not available yet

The problem is, that some people do not have access to their adult functions at will. Instead, they may go blank, access an inherited inner critic, or even more commonly – access a child part who may be playing at being an adult. Telling them to just access their adult is like telling them to just be able to fly.

To help these people access their adult functions, I recommend the following steps. Please note, the following is a bridge that I developed – while many of the steps have been shown to be effective, the entirety of the steps have not (to the best of my knowledge).
- Access a witnessing position, if necessary. If you already know how to distinguish your internal positions, skip to the next step and access the adult position you need.

- Borrow an adult function. You may “borrow” this from a safe adult in your life, a mentor, an older sibling, a future version of yourself, a spiritual figure, a value, or even a written plan. Borrow whatever you need – warmth, direction, etc.
- Put on the adult hat as an apprentice. Now, in this position, figure out what you would want to say or do – and then do at least a part of that.
- Return the adult hat, noticing what you borrowed and what you were able to do on your own (even if it’s only 5%).
This is a borrowed figure, so you’re still making the choice. The longer version of this exercise can be found in my Inner Child Self-Love Reparenting Guide .

You don’t have to have trustworthy people in your history. Just imagine a good adult. See if you can imagine what they would say/do in your situation, with your history, limitations, options, etc. If you can’t imagine good, imagine the least cruel thing you can. Once you’ve found something good, try it, don’t keep doing the exercise.

It can be helpful to use borrowing when you’re in the adult position and not knowing what a decent adult would do, especially when it seems like any response will be retaliatory, defensive, collapsing, leaving, etc. Borrow a decent adult’s response. You may still feel young when you do it, it’s okay, you’ll become an adult after you act like one.
Let the child speak without handing over the steering wheel

It is possible to regress psychologically and allow those younger states to talk, but still maintain adult judgement. You don't have to turn that judgement over to someone else or literally become younger. You just get to tap into those feelings of wonder, play, sensation, vulnerability, need or whatever it is you feel you need less responsibility.

"It is okay for a younger part of me to talk. But I understand that the adult in me is always going to be here, evaluating, protecting me and stopping me if needed. I am not going to replace my adult judgement with any child state, guide, recording or person."

This way you get the benefits of being young; curiosity, spontaneity, play, sensation, the ability to state your needs, to feel easily etc without any of the negatives of being a child, like obeying, being helpless, being scolded, the lack of good judgement etc.
Love doesn’t have to wait for trust

If the younger position doesn’t believe you love him/her yet, you can still love him/her. You can love him/her even if the trust position doesn’t trust your promises yet, even if he/she remembers that you haven’t been able to protect him/her yet.
You can start with something like, “Okay. I believe that you don’t believe me. I still love you though. It’s okay if you don’t love me yet. Tell me what doesn’t feel safe to you.”

Respond to complaints by hearing the truth in them and by responding to them, as well as by providing the other evidence of love: preparing and serving meals, setting limits to protect him/her, taking him/her to appointments, keeping promises, admitting when you haven’t been able to live up to your promises, etc. If the younger position attacks you in his/her mind, admit that you haven’t been able to protect him/her yet, work on it, and let him/her know when you’ve made a change. Show your love by not retaliating, but don’t substitute not retaliating for loving the younger position.

Keep in mind that the position that made the vow and the position that blames the child for not accepting the vow may be two separate positions, or they may be the same position, or they may be a blend. Don’t go by chronological age.

Imagine that you are in court and the defendant is you, only a few years younger. Would it be of any value to try and understand why you did whatever it was you did? Would it help to try and appreciate what options you felt you had? Would any useful insight be gained by considering the consequences of your actions? Whilst acknowledging the harm you may have caused, and working to address and repair that harm, would simply punishing you make any difference to the person you were when you committed the offence?
The two-hand practice

So here is a simple easy little bit of body work that will help you get in touch with your inner child. All you have to do is place one hand in the center of your chest. Remember your heart is there and it's full of love. Now place your other hand just below that, at your solar plexis, that is where you can relate to your child.

Now begin sending love down to your child from your heart and just notice what comes up for you. It doesn't matter if something comes up or not, if there is resistance come it with love, if you feel or see something come it with love. Just communicate with your child from your heart.
Now remember when you do this, Love is on top and your child is on the bottom and you as the adult are right there with them.
The Nurturer

One of the most important things you can do as a Nurturer is to enjoy your children. To sit back and not feel like you have to move their feelings, but actually say to them, “I’m really glad you are here in this moment.” Children need to be enjoyed, not just consoled when they are hurt.
“I know it’s okay for you to feel the way you are feeling.”
“I want you to know that I’m here for you.”
“Right now, you don’t have to do anything.”
“You are not too much.”
“It’s okay to be small. You can be small here with me.”
“It’s okay to be angry. You can be angry here.”
“It’s okay to be sad. You can be sad here.”
“I’m going to be here for you.”
The Protector
Identify your protector and try to bring a bit of their warmth.

Then set boundaries together - it can be anything from, 'I will leave that conversation', 'I will stop texting that person', 'I will eat today', 'I will get some sleep tonight', 'I will do x', or, 'I won't put you in the position of having to deal with x '.

It's important to note that lots of people do ICW but it's often fluffy brouhaha - they talk to their IC, but they don't actually do the things they need to in their adult life. So in order to build trust with your IC, you need to do the thing . And deal with the fallout if you don't.

If you can't bring any warmth to the Protector, that's okay, just work with them on doing protective things for your child. Make sure they are attainable. If you don't do them, work out why - was it fear, exhaustion, lack of skills, lack of X, poor planning, etc.? Also, make sure that doing them is actually helpful - don't just be ticking things off a list.
The Leader, Guide, or Guru
Working with the Leader function, who provides direction. You can give it the name you like: Leader, Guide, Guru, Wise One, Sage, Inner Teacher, Director, Higher Adult, etc.

Invite it to give direction in an effective way, not in a way that expects you to be perfectly disciplined and not have any needs. Ask it to help you find a way to do the adult thing and ask for help, express a preference, allow a safe person to see your imperfections, etc. Find ways to get your need for closeness met without punishing the other person for needing space. Etc.

Affirmations to support the Leader may include: “We are not only here to feel good.” “We are here to become whole.” “We are here to belong to life itself, not only to people who approve of us.” “We are here to serve truth, beauty, love, God, source, nature, universe, dharma, Tao, the benefit of all beings.” Etc.

Begin working with the adult function, perhaps beginning with protection, then warmth. Be sure that the direction serves your child’s growth, but doesn’t deprive your child of necessary care, play, support, etc.
Working with protectors
If this language is familiar to you, feel free to use it.
Most people assume when approaching their inner child that the first thing they’ll encounter is…their inner child.

But more often than not, what you actually experience is numbness, cynicism, anger, hunger, the sudden urge to check your phone, a sexual urge, mental planning, sleepiness, dissociation, or the simple thought that “this is stupid”. These are all common manifestations of protectors.

One of the most important protectors to become aware of when approaching your inner child is your inherited parent. This is the voice of your parent(s) that you internalized as a child, based on how they treated you. This is not the same as your inner adult (Nurturer, Protector, Leader/Guru) that you will eventually build up. Often this inherited parent acts as a critic or warden, telling your inner child not to cry, not to be “needy”, not to embarrass them, not to be too independent, etc. So when you begin talking to your child in a new, loving way, this voice may jump in to say that what you’re doing is “fake”.
It’s okay, I see what you’re doing. Can I ask you what you’re afraid would happen if you let this go?

Now be patient, and listen. It may be that they’re afraid that you’ll fall for your bullshit again, or that you’ll spiritualize this issue, or feel your pain, or forgive someone too early, or believe your fantasies again, or leave them hanging once the therapy session is over.
Now, thank the protective part, and ask them what they need from you to feel 1% safer.

99% of the time, the answer will be some non-spiritual thing like maintaining a boundary, doing a certain task, eating properly, holding back from sending a text, or sleeping, or reaching out to a therapist, or acknowledging that you do, in fact, owe someone money.
Protection that knows when to stop scanning
Does anyone here practice the following sequence to “embody” Protector?
(1) orient self (look around, feel support, etc.),
(2) assess situation (what do you know, not know, need to check out?),
(3) differentiate between actual/real dangers, uncertainty, past dangers or imagined dangers,
(4) set boundaries (just one, proportional to danger level; move, stop, delay, ask, leave, get support, etc.),
(5) verify sufficient safety (based on reality), and finally
(6) stand down and rest.

Seems to me that this would be a “mature” Protector. For example, it wouldn’t be afraid to say, “I don’t know”, or to ask another human being, or to delay interpreting what’s going on, or to use a no-trance practice. I want to be able to “do” this. I am learning discernment and to quit scanning the room after taking appropriate action.
Inner child reparenting

Client, I want to talk about the connection between the reparenting therapy you are doing, and the self hypnosis. I think it can be a perfect fit. So, while you are in hypnosis, you might summon the child (this can be any age, image, posture, voice, memory, emotion, vulnerable self, or no child at all. If there is no child, just work with whatever protector you do have, either in the form of a sensation, feeling, or preference).
If there is a child that appears, don’t feel like you have to do anything with them. Just be with them.

See if you can tell the child: “Little one, you don’t have to do anything for me, you don’t have to tell me anything, you don’t even have to be healed. You don’t have to impress me. Just tell me if there’s something you need to help you feel less alone in this world.

It can be anything. Need to warm yourself by a fire? need to play? need protection? need to grieve? need to be angry? need food? rest? a boundary? a relationship? need to stop fantasizing? need to stop working so hard? need me to keep a promise to you for one day?
Don’t rush the repair
Find a younger you /protector/feeling/signal in your body that needs tending to and then:
Prepare yourself to do the tending (Get yourself into a place where you have time, privacy, support etc. Be as adult as you can)
Ask for permission to move closer or what is needed (warmth, space, words, silence, no contact etc)
Do something to meet one of the needs you find when you move closer. Don’t try to fix it all.
Wait a while for the effect of what you have done to sink in.
Reconnect with that part of you ( don’t expect it to become one with you, go away, or be happy, just connect if it wants to)
Rest a while and then reassess to see how things are now.

Your aim is not to make it all good as new but good as you. Feel free to change the language if the part talk is not useful, think signal, feeling, younger you or anything that helps you connect with the issue
Play and rest still need an adult present

It is important for reparenting to remember to have fun. It's really okay to let your younger states enjoy playing with things that interest them. Touch textures, draw, move your body, talk to your plushie in a different voice, as long as you can keep reality testing intact and remember that you are not actually a child/pet/doll/whatever and are not owned, it's okay to recover your play ability.

Non-dominant hand dialogue

If speaking or visualization doesn’t work, try writing. Have your non-dominant hand write as your child/protector (even if your handwriting looks a little awkward), and have your dominant hand answer as you. For example, your non-dominant hand might write, “I don’t trust you.” Answer with your dominant hand, “I hear that you don’t trust me, but I love you, and I want to know where I’ve let you down. I won’t ask you to trust me, but I want to hear you out and make one promise to you that I will keep today.” Your non-dominant hand might respond, “What promise?” Your dominant hand might write, “To eat, or to clean my desk, or to not text someone who makes me feel unsafe.”
